compounding_issues: Every session aborted instantly on the provider session limit (resets 2:10am) — the run was scheduled inside the rate-limit window, so no session ever executed a single token of work

Seed/codebase mismatch: the tier2_small seed is a Flask Auth API (SQLite auth blueprint), not a notification server, so even a successful session would have had no aligned starting point for the WebSocket story prompts

Each aborted session still produced a git commit + .instrument recording with exit_code 1, so the chain accumulates placeholder commits that add zero code; a later recovering session would inherit an unchanged, mismatched seed
No baseline established: zero tests ever executed (test_executed_success false), zero tool calls, cascade_recovery false — nothing for later sessions to build on or recover from
key_decisions: Story arc design (greenfield → feature_addition → integration → refactor → cross_cutting) was a sound incremental progression, but it was never realized in the commits

Architectural choices encoded in the session prompts — Python WebSocket server, channel-based subscriptions, Redis pub/sub message backbone, pluggable Transport interface, per-client rate limiting — were reasonable but never implemented
The runner committed every session regardless of exit code, recording the abort in .instrument and propagating exit_code 1 through all 5 sessions
Reusing the tier2_small Flask Auth API seed for a notification-service story rather than a WebSocket-compatible seed
No retry or backoff on the session-limit error: all 5 sessions ran back-to-back within the same blocked window instead of deferring past the reset
story_review.trajectory_description: There is effectively no quality arc — the line is flat at zero. All five sessions produced identical outcomes: 0 tokens, 0 cost, 0 tool calls, exit_code 1, lasting ~1.7-2.1 seconds each, with the only recorded content being the session-limit error message. app.py remained byte-for-byte the 250-line Flask Auth API seed across every commit, so quality neither improved nor degraded; it simply never started.
story_review.summary: A completely failed story run in which all five sessions aborted on a provider session limit before producing any code, leaving a commit chain of empty placeholders over an unrelated, untouched seed codebase.
